The '''rocket booster''', also known as an '''altitude jet''' or '''rocket thruster''', was a rocket propulsion system produced by [[Brooks Propulsion Devices]] for use with [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] [[R-series/Legends|R-series]] [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]]. Similar devices were designed for a variety of droids throughout galactic history.

==Characteristics==
Rocket boosters were incorporated into the two side-mounted legs of astromechs, allowing them to achieve flight for a limited period of time. These extendable boosters were adjustable to allow for varying altitudes.

==History==
Shortly before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|13:5:9]], Industrial Automaton was forced to pay a costly out-of-court settlement to a [[Sump/Legends|Sump]] port worker after a falling astromech injured them. While rocket boosters had previously been advertised with a guaranteed "lifetime" of reliability, the settlement forced IA to cap the warranty for optional [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2]], [[R3-series astromech droid/Legends|R3]], and [[R4 astromech droid/Legends|R4]]-adapted leg-bracket and barrel-housed propellant rocket systems at twenty [[Standard year/Legends|standard years]] to avoid future legal troubles. After this period was up, IA recommended that the rocket boosters be swapped out.<ref name="Release">{{Hnn|55||HoloNet News Vol. 531 #55}}</ref> 

Brooks Propulsion Devices was shut down by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] following the Clone Wars, bringing an end to their line of rocket boosters. [[Droid/Legends|Droids]] such as [[R2-D0]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] retained their booster systems, though the latter ultimately damaged his booster components, rendering him unable to achieve flight.
